source.basis: Existing local Demo implementation, not a new interpretation or approval of the official website

reusableImplementation: CatalogProductGrid: render caller-provided items in input order without modifying data
Explicit empty state and escaped text
CatalogSection: static title, category labels and product-grid composition
implementationRules: Independent use requires appearance=onepiece and an explicit CSS import; the default legacy appearance requires caller styles
Grid remains two columns at all widths; media box is 122px high with object-fit:contain
Card reading order is image, category/code, title, release, optional CTA text
Source density guidance is not implemented as responsive behavior; never require the host to invent eight records
notSupported: Category selection, filtering, requests, navigation and pagination
Animated grid/list switching or official motion timing
Desktop four-column / mobile two-column responsive parity
Full brand typography, expressive design, accessibility or complete host certification
knownLimitations: Category buttons are disabled and have no selection event; the first category is always active, so another active item can produce two active labels
The onepiece section CSS hides description and label; CTA is non-interactive text
A missing image URL has a text placeholder; failed image requests have no built-in fallback, and the Demo global error handler is not packaged
Poppins is not bundled; system fallbacks change typography
Only surface and mediaRadius are generated DTCG tokens; other dimensions remain CSS literals
Product images, official fonts and reference screenshots are not included; the consumer supplies permitted assets
hostResponsibilities: Keep business data, item order, routes, selection state, requests and native interactions in the host
Do not replace functional host filters with CatalogSection static labels
Do not infer Taro compatibility from the Vue peer dependency
Use as a design reference outside Vue Web, not as an installed native adapter
verificationBoundary: Tarball and SSR tests reuse the locally installed Vue peer runtime. They do not verify a fresh install, browser layout, image-network behavior or real-host integration. No legacy QA verdict or failed learning run is superseded.
